name: VoIP push (PushKit) and call-style wakeups
plain: A special push that wakes the app for a call; iOS demands it shows a call UI right away.
meaning: Used for real-time calls, the strongest wake-up either platform offers. Misuse for silent tracking got apps cut off on iOS 13, so both platforms now tie it to a visible call screen.

android.permission: MANAGE_OWN_CALLS or telecom ConnectionService; USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT; FOREGROUND_SERVICE_PHONE_CALL (API 34)
android.prompt_ui: Call UI; full screen intent needs grant on 14+ for non calling apps
android.persistence: High priority FCM data message wakes the app even in Doze
android.store_policy: Play policy: full-screen intent only for calling and alarm apps (Android 14)
android.note: No separate payload limit beyond FCM 4 KB

ios.permission: voip UIBackgroundModes; PushKit VoIP certificate; apns-push-type voip; CallKit
ios.persistence: From iOS 13 each VoIP push must report a CallKit call; repeated failure stops further VoIP pushes
ios.store_policy: App Review 2.5.4; VoIP only for real VoIP calling
ios.note: VoIP payload up to 5120 bytes; apns-priority 10

limits.headline: Can wake the app right away for a call, if it shows a call screen
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when someone calls you through the app
can: Wake the app for an incoming call, even when closed
Show the call screen on iPhone with CallKit
Use a full screen call alert on Android
cannot: Use call pushes for non call alerts on iPhone; Apple requires a call screen right away
Show a full screen alert on Android 14 or newer for non calling apps without your grant
Send more than 5 KB on iPhone, or 4 KB on Android
limits.differs: iPhone requires Apple approval and a call screen at once. Android uses normal high priority push plus a call screen.

story.what_it_is: A special push that wakes an app for a call, and must show a call screen right away.

marketing.name: PushKit and VoIP
marketing.pitch: Apple documents VoIP pushes as the way for calling apps to wake and show an incoming call screen.

story.for_you: Your phone rings with a full call screen, even if the app was closed. If an app wakes this way without a call, iOS will stop letting it.
story.for_makers: Makers get the strongest wake up for real time calls. Misuse as a secret wake up got apps cut off, so both systems now tie it to a visible call.

use_cases.example: A WhatsApp or FaceTime style call rings your locked phone.
A group video chat pings you to join a live room.
A voice chat for a squad rings you when your friends start a match.
A contact center app rings a work phone with a customer call.
A telehealth app rings the patient as the doctor joins the visit.
A smart doorbell rings you like a call when someone is at the door.
A driver call bridge rings a hidden number for the rider.

risks: Past abuse as a covert wake up
Can pull the app out of sleep
story.android_note: On Android, full screen alerts need a grant for non calling apps.
story.ios_note: iOS needs a call screen right away through CallKit.

technical_bounds: iOS revokes pushes if apps do not report a call

abuse: Using VoIP pushes as a covert wakeup

history.change: Every VoIP push must report a CallKit call or PushKit pushes stop
USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT limited to calling and alarm apps; FGS type phoneCall requires its own permission

refs.label: Apple: Responding to VoIP notifications from PushKit
